## What we know

- **Name:** 勺园 / 弘雅园 / 集贤院 Shao Yuan, Hongya Yuan, Jixian Yuan (S1215, S1216, S02, S23, S1201, S03 · confidence B)
- **In English:** Ladle Garden (Ming), later the envoys' and officials' house (S1215, S1216, S02, S23, S1201, S03)
- **What it was:** a neighbouring imperial or princely garden outside the garden walls (S1215, S1216, S02, S23, S1201, S03 · confidence B)
- **In 1860:** the officials' duty house 集贤院 (from 1801); on 18 Sept 1860 Parkes and some thirty other prisoners were held at its 提督公所 (S1215; S02 p.187: local tradition); after 1860 abandoned (S1215); 'burned with 圆明园' (S1201 lead) (S1215, S1216, S02, S23, S1201, S03)
- **Where:** today's name 勺园 of PKU's south-west complex (osm node 13787235273): C; Malone's sketch puts 集贤院 east of 畅春园's east wall, south of the old 勺园 / Yenching; its extent, a circle of 90 m, is assumed (S1215, S1216, S02, S23, S1201, S03 · confidence C)
- **Note:** 米万钟's 勺园 c.1612-14 (S1216); Macartney lodged there 2 Aug 1793 (S02 p.166; S1215), Amherst 1816. Its Taihu rock in the 赛克勒 museum court; 'Mo Er Ken Yuan' (S02 p.107). Wording on 1860 kept factual. (S1215, S1216, S02, S23, S1201, S03)
